function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

The user wants the temperature forecast for New York next week. We need to use the Open-Meteo API via the provided function. We'll need to get the latitude and longitude for New York City. NYC coordinates: approximately 40.7128° N, -74.0060° W. So latitude=40.7128, longitude=-74.0060.

We want the temperature forecast for next week. The Open-Meteo API can provide daily forecasts. We might want to fetch daily maximum/minimum temperatures for the next 7 days. The API endpoint: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". Parameters: latitude, longitude, daily="temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min", timezone="America/New_York", start_date, end_date. But we don't have to specify dates; we can just ask for the next 7 days. The API supports "forecast_days" parameter? Actually, the API uses "daily" and "start_date" and "end_date". We can set start_date to today, end_date to today+7 days. But we don't know today's date. We could just request the next 7 days from now. The API may return the next 7 days by default if not specified? Let's check typical usage: For daily forecast, you can specify "daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min" and "timezone=America/New_York". It will return daily values for the next 7 days by default. So we can call the API with those parameters.

Thus we need to call the function:

{
  url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
  params: {
    latitude: 40.7128,
    longitude: -74.0060,
    daily: "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min",
    timezone: "America/New_York"
  }
}

We don't need headers. The function signature includes optional headers but defaults to JSON. So we can just pass the params.

We'll then parse the returned JSON. The structure likely contains "daily": { "time": [...], "temperature_2m_max": [...], "temperature_2m_min": [...] }. We'll extract the dates and temperatures.

Then we need to respond to the user with the forecast. The user asked: "كم ستكون درجة الحرارة الاسبوع القادم هناك؟" which translates to "What will the temperature be next week there?" They probably want a summary of the forecast. We can give them the max/min temperatures for each day.

We also need to consider the user's language: Arabic. So we should respond in Arabic. Provide a friendly answer.

Thus steps:

1. Call the function with the appropriate parameters.
2. Receive the result.
3. Parse the JSON.
4. Format the output in Arabic.

Let's do that.
